definition: MBROLA is speech synthesis software as a worldwide collaborative project.
details: The MBROLA project web page provides diphone databases for many spoken languages. The MBROLA software is not a complete speech synthesis system for all those languages; the text must first be transformed into phoneme and prosodic information in MBROLA's format, and separate software (e.g. eSpeakNG) is necessary.

explainer.lead: MBROLA is speech synthesis software run as a worldwide collaborative project. Its web page provides diphone databases for many spoken languages.

tiers.eli5: It's a voice-building tool: you feed it the sounds of speech in its own format and it produces the spoken audio.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers must first convert text into phoneme and prosodic information in MBROLA's format and pair it with separate software such as eSpeakNG; MBROLA alone is not a complete speech synthesis system for those languages.
tiers.paperLevel: A diphone-based synthesiser; it requires phoneme and prosodic input in its own format and does not perform text-to-phoneme conversion itself.

explainer.example: A pipeline uses eSpeakNG to turn text into phonemes, then MBROLA with a language's diphone database to produce the audio.
